question: What can public NFRDI, IUCN, thesis-catalog and planning records support about Lake Buhi and adjacent sinarapan habitats, without inventing a complete fish checklist?

sourcesReviewed.citation: Gamez, M. S. (2025). FFRDC presents findings on stock assessment of Lake Buhi. Fisearch, 7(1), 14.
sourcesReviewed.access: Official NFRDI repository metadata and full one-page newsletter article reviewed. It says results of the 2023-2024 Lake Buhi assessment were presented in Buhi on March 11, 2025. Project components included sinarapan morphology/genetics and reproduction, cage aquaculture productivity/cost, and ichthyoplankton abundance/distribution. It does not publish the underlying fish-species checklist, station-by-taxon table, sample counts or voucher links.
sourcesReviewed.reuse: No item-specific data/app reuse terms found. Attribution and link only; publication approval remains false.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Soliman et al. (2021). Mistichthys luzonensis. The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species 2021: e.T13586A117405712. Assessment date: 2020-09-07.
sourcesReviewed.access: Official DOI landing page could not be retrieved. The complete assessment text and copyright notice were read in the linked ResearchGate copy. Its range narrative names Lake Buhi, Lake Bato, Lake Danao (Polangui, Albay), and lakelets Manapao, Katugday, Paguiriron and Makuao. It distinguishes four natural Camarines Sur populations and two direct-transfer populations, plus the Albay Danao record. It discusses February 2020 aging-study captures and misidentification of look-alikes; the range narrative is not a station/event dataset.
sourcesReviewed.reuse: The assessment itself permits educational/non-commercial reproduction with attribution and requires prior permission for commercial reproduction/reposting. No Bangwit content or data publication approval is given.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Baquiran, N. B. (2011). Useful and edible fauna of lake and lakelets of Lake Buhi, Camarines Sur [Undergraduate thesis]. Manila Central University.
sourcesReviewed.access: HERDIN abstract and MCU thesis catalog reviewed. The abstract describes collection during October and December 2011 by hand, sakag push-net and diving, with identification at the National Museum. It states 23 fauna species but the category counts say 8 fish, 4 crustaceans and eleven (12) mollusks. The thesis is held at MCU-LRC; no full text or species names were retrieved.
sourcesReviewed.reuse: No item-specific license identified. No species data can be derived from the abstract-only record.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Japan International Cooperation Agency. (2023). Data Collection Survey for National Water Resources Development and Management Plan: Final Report, Chapter 4, p. 4-272.
sourcesReviewed.access: Indexed report excerpt reviewed. It says seven native fish species besides sinarapan have been observed in Lake Buhi and names four examples (Redigobius dispar, Channa striata, and Anabas testudineus plus local name Atas); its footnote attributes the biodiversity passage to DENR's 2015 Integrated Bicol River Basin Management and Development Master Plan. The underlying master-plan passage/method was not independently retrieved, and the full 26.7 MB report could not be opened in the web review tool.
sourcesReviewed.reuse: No item-specific app/data reuse terms verified. Research lead only; no public-app publication approval.

sourcesReviewed.citation: DA-NFRDI (2025). Saving Lake Buhi's sinarapan: Safeguarding biodiversity and local livelihoods.
sourcesReviewed.access: Previously reviewed official NFRDI feature describing its 2023-2024 assessment of Lake Buhi and adjacent waters. It reports verified sinarapan in analyzed Lake Manapao samples and none among analyzed samples from Buhi, Bato, Danao, Katugday and Makuao. It omits per-waterbody effort, exact dates, sample counts, vouchers and detection sensitivity. This is another public summary of the same assessment program, not an independent study from the Fisearch article.
sourcesReviewed.reuse: No item-specific content reuse license verified; summary only, no app publication approval.

crossSourceAssessment.nfrdiAssessment: The 2023-2024 assessment is a strong lead to a completed government fisheries assessment, but the two accessible NFRDI communications do not expose its complete fish inventory or supporting sample/voucher data. The 2025 Fisearch newsletter and September feature are communications about the same assessment, not independent replications.
crossSourceAssessment.sinarapanRangeAndDetection: The 2021 IUCN assessment (assessed 2020-09-07) describes a broader historical/recent-at-assessment-time Bicol range that includes Buhi, Bato, Katugday, Manapao, Makuao, Paguiriron and Lake Danao in Polangui. The later 2023-2024 NFRDI summary reports a verified result only at Manapao among its analyzed samples and sample-level non-detections at five named waters. Do not collapse these time-bounded findings into permanent presence/absence; exact effort and detection limits are missing in the public NFRDI summary.
crossSourceAssessment.thesisLead: Baquiran's 2011 fauna thesis could supply an older fish/crustacean/mollusk inventory, but the abstract contains an arithmetic/wording inconsistency and withholds all taxon names. It is not usable as a species list until the full thesis and tables are obtained and reconciled.
crossSourceAssessment.secondaryNativeFishClaim: The JICA report's seven-native-fish statement is explicitly footnoted to a DENR 2015 master plan; only four examples are named and survey methods/events are not exposed in the excerpt. Treat the cited master plan as the primary-retrieval target, not the JICA excerpt as occurrence rows.
crossSourceAssessment.waterbodyIdentity: Lake Danao in Polangui, Albay is the Bicol waterbody in the IUCN assessment. Do not confuse it with the separately studied Lake Danao in Ormoc City, Leyte. Lake Buhi and its smaller lakelets also remain separate waterbody units.
crossSourceAssessment.appReadiness: Research leads only. No new species, occurrence, absence, population, native-status, geometry, diet, legal or safety assertions and no public-app rows are admitted. The primary NFRDI assessment tables, full Baquiran thesis and DENR 2015 source remain retrieval needs.

disposition.reason: The NFRDI summaries lack public station-level data, the IUCN range evidence is time-bounded and conflicts with newer bounded sampling, Baquiran's list is unavailable and internally inconsistent, and the JICA fish count traces to an inaccessible underlying DENR plan.

nextAction: Continue Bicol inland-water screening with Lake Danao (Polangui, Albay) and the separately named Buhi lakelets; retrieve the cited DENR 2015 plan and seek the underlying NFRDI Lake Buhi assessment tables and Baquiran 2011 thesis in parallel. Keep the Leyte Lake Danao study out of the Bicol batch and continue other regional habitats without waiting for these documents.

sources.supports: Official NFRDI repository citation, 2023-2024 Lake Buhi project scope and presentation date, including absence of a checklist/table in this one-page summary.
Full one-page Fisearch article text; summarizes assessment components but supplies no species inventory or sampling event crosswalk.
Official NFRDI account of analyzed sinarapan samples from Manapao and bounded non-detections from Buhi, Bato, Danao, Katugday and Makuao, with the stated public-detail limitations.
IUCN 2021 conservation assessment (assessed 2020) and its Bicol waterbody range narrative, as read via a full-text copy; separate retrieval of the official DOI endpoint was unavailable.
Accessible full-text copy of IUCN assessment, date, waterbody names, sampling/misidentification context, assessors and the assessment's reuse notice.
HERDIN abstract for Baquiran 2011 thesis, collection months/methods, identification institution, aggregate fauna claims and internal count inconsistency.
MCU's completed-thesis catalog confirms title, author and year; it does not contain the thesis species tables.
Indexed Lake Buhi secondary report excerpt naming partial fish examples, seven-native-fish claim, underlying DENR 2015 citation and July 2023 report pagination.
Official IUCN terms for textual-content reproduction and third-party copyright; the species assessment's own copyright notice is retained as the item-specific statement.
